Task: Bull marking for flooring of wet areas along with bore packing
QC check: All MEP works are completed as per the drawings.
What to measure or judge: Every MEP item in the drawing is present: floor traps, pipe stubs, conduits, boxes.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: from the sweep, Gemini lists the MEP points it sees per wall and on the floor and compares with the drawing's list.
How it would work: Same detector family as ID 317: detect the visible MEP items on the rectified walls and the top-down floor and compare count and positions with the plumbing and electrical layouts. Items concealed in chases or under the screed cannot be verified from images.
Fallback or upgrade: ATTEST: MEP supervisor sign-off on a marked-up drawing.
Target tolerance (typical; confirm again: All visible items present; position ± 50 mm

QC check: Balcony/ Bathroom: 2 day water ponding test is done and is found to be ok.
What to measure or judge: Water level held for 48 h; no damp on the soffit below.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: two photos 48 h apart with a tape at the waterline, plus one of the ceiling below.
How it would work: Two time-stamped photos from the same spot 48 h apart with a tape or a mark at the waterline, plus one of the ceiling below. The vision model compares the waterline with the mark and reads the soffit for damp patches. The app enforces the 48 h gap.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP close-up of the waterline and the mark.
Target tolerance (typical; confirm again: No drop beyond evaporation (a few mm); no damp below

QC check: Balcony/ Bathroom: Screed concrete Curing done as per standards
What to measure or judge: Curing maintained for the required days.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: one photo per curing day showing the wet or ponded screed.
How it would work: One photo per day for the curing period; the vision model confirms a wet or ponded surface and the timestamps prove the duration.
Fallback or upgrade: MANUAL record.

QC check: Balcony/ Bathroom: Screed concrete mix is as per specifications
What to measure or judge: Screed mix proportion at batching.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: short video of the screed batching at mixing.
How it would work: Same evidence flow as ID 299, for the screed batching.
Fallback or upgrade: MANUAL: cube test records where required.

Task: Bull marking for flooring of wet areas along with bore packing
QC check: Balcony/ Bathroom: Slope of the flooring is checked and is ok.
What to measure or judge: Floor slope toward the drain after tiling.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: phone laid on the tiles at two or three points, as for ID 206.
How it would work: Same as ID 206, on the finished tiles: the phone laid flat at two or three points reads the slope to about 0.1°.
Fallback or upgrade: ATTEST: short video of water running to the drain.
Target tolerance (typical; confirm again: Slope at or above spec, toward the drain

Task: Bull marking for flooring along with Colour and pattern for tiles having been approved by Customer and surface preparation for dry areas
QC check: Before tiling, SFL (Standard Floor Level) should be transferred from main entrance, passage, or corridor based on site conditions.
What to measure or judge: SFL mark present on the room's walls and at the same height as the reference at the entrance.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: Gemini finds the SFL mark on each wall in the sweep; heights compared with the entrance mark.
How it would work: The vision model looks for the SFL line on each wall in the sweep; pencil or chalk marks are faint from the room centre. Height consistency with the entrance mark needs a common frame across rooms.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP photo of the mark with a tape from the slab.
Target tolerance (typical; confirm again: Mark present; height within 5 mm of the reference

Task: Chasing, Conduit fixing, Door Frame Fixing, Grill Fixing and Chicken Mesh
QC check: Cement mortar mix is found to be as per the contract.
What to measure or judge: Mix proportion and materials at batching.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: short video of the batching (gauge boxes, bags) at mixing.
How it would work: A short video of the batching: gauge boxes or bags counted per batch, sand type, water. The vision model can count bags and boxes; it cannot verify a ratio once mixed.
Fallback or upgrade: MANUAL: cube or field test records where the contract requires them.

QC check: Client to give a go ahead on the location of the plumbing points.
What to measure or judge: Client approval of the plumbing point locations recorded.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: client approval step in the app, as for ID 199.
How it would work: Same approval flow as ID 199: the marked points (sweep frames or the plumbing layout) go to the client for an OTP or signature approval.
Fallback or upgrade: Site-visit sign-off photo.

Stage: Casting the lintels,staircase, blockwork upto the slab level
QC check: Dia of main bars (in both the direction), spacing of bars as per structural drawing.
What to measure or judge: Bar diameter and spacing in both directions against the structural drawing.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: photo of the cage with a tape across the bars; spacing from the photo, diameter from a close-up.
How it would work: One photo of the cage with a tape or a 100 mm tag laid on it. Spacing reads from the photo to about ±5 mm; diameter needs a close-up (8, 10 and 12 mm bars differ by 2 mm, which needs about 0.3 mm per pixel). The vision model counts the bars and reads the tape.
Fallback or upgrade: MANUAL: the SE reads the diameter from the bar marking or with a vernier.
Target tolerance (typical; confirm again: Spacing ± 10 mm; diameter as per drawing

Stage: Casting the lintels,staircase, blockwork upto the slab level
QC check: Dia of main bars (in both the direction), spacing of bars as per structural drawing.
What to measure or judge: Bar diameter and spacing against the structural drawing (lintel).
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: same as ID 47, on the lintel cage.
How it would work: Same detector as ID 47, on the lintel cage.
Fallback or upgrade: MANUAL: diameter from the bar marking.
Target tolerance (typical; confirm again: Spacing ± 10 mm; diameter as per drawing

Stage: Column rising, blockwork upto lintel level
QC check: Diagonals have been checked and wall are found to be at right angles.
What to measure or judge: Room diagonals equal; corner angles 90°.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: corner angles from the sweep as for ID 318; laser meter on both diagonals when flagged.
How it would work: Same detector as ID 318: corner angles from the recovered floor plan, about ±1°. Equal diagonals to 10 mm on a 3 m room need 0.2°, so this is screening only.
Fallback or upgrade: BT-TOOL laser meter: two diagonal readings give the squareness exactly.

Stage: Column rising, blockwork upto lintel level
QC check: During blockwork, keep 1" extra clearance in height and width for window and door openings.
What to measure or judge: Opening width and height against the frame size plus 25 mm.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: photo with the tape across the opening; the gyro's ±25 mm is too coarse for a 25 mm clearance.
How it would work: Same detector as ID 125, measuring the raw opening before the frames go in. The gyro's ±20–30 mm at 3 m equals the clearance itself, so it can only flag openings that are clearly tight or oversized.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP with the tape across the opening. Tags on the datum line bring the gyro to about ±10 mm.

QC check: Electrical fixing is well finished and free from any gaps at ceiling
What to measure or judge: Ceiling fittings (fan hooks, light points, boxes) flush and finished, no gaps.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: upward band of the sweep; Gemini checks the ceiling fittings for gaps and finish.
How it would work: The upward band of the sweep shows the ceiling fittings; the vision model checks each for gaps, exposed wires and finish. Needs a band near +90° so the ceiling centre is covered.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP close-up where the model is unsure.

Stage: Casting the lintels,staircase, blockwork upto the slab level
QC check: Exposed steel if any, Is packed as per standards
What to measure or judge: Exposed reinforcement at lintel ends or faces; packing done where it was exposed.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: Gemini flags exposed rebar in the sweep frames around the lintels.
How it would work: The vision model flags exposed rebar (rust-coloured bars against concrete) in the frames around the lintels; a flagged spot after packing should read as a patched surface. Small exposures far from the tripod can be missed.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP close-up of each flagged spot.

Stage: Casting the lintels,staircase, blockwork upto the slab level
QC check: Exposed steel if any, Is packed as per standards
What to measure or judge: Exposed reinforcement on the staircase after concreting.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: same as ID 42, on the staircase frames.
How it would work: Same detector as ID 42, run on the staircase frames (soffit, waist, risers).
Fallback or upgrade: TAP close-up of each flagged spot.

Task: Electrical Point marking, Plumbing Point marking and Bull Marking for plastering
QC check: Exposed steel if any, Is packed as per standards
What to measure or judge: Exposed slab or lintel steel in chases, packed before plastering.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: same as ID 42, after chasing.
How it would work: Same detector as ID 42, run after chasing and conduit fixing.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP close-up of each flagged spot.

QC check: Haunching has been done in wet areas
What to measure or judge: Concrete haunch (fillet) at every wall-floor junction in wet areas.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: downward band of the sweep; Gemini checks the haunch at every wall-floor junction.
How it would work: The downward band of the sweep shows the wall-floor junction all round; the vision model checks for the haunch on every wall. Haunch size can be read from the rectified wall if your spec gives one.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP close-up at a junction.
Inputs the prompt needs: Haunch size from spec, if any.

QC check: Mortar is mixed with bonding agent as per the contract specifications.
What to measure or judge: Bonding agent added to the mortar at the specified dose.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: short video of the batching showing the bonding agent container and its dosing.
How it would work: Same evidence flow as ID 299; the video must show the bonding agent container and its dosing.
Fallback or upgrade: MANUAL: consumption against the area plastered.

QC check: No hollow sound on the tile when tapped
What to measure or judge: Hollow (debonded) tiles found by tap sound.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: tap each tile with a coin while recording; the tap sound is classified hollow or solid.
How it would work: The SE taps each tile with a coin or a small mallet while the phone records a short video; the tap sounds are classified hollow or solid and the frames show which tile was tapped. Needs a labelled sample set from your tiles and adhesive.
Fallback or upgrade: MANUAL tap test by the SE, marking hollow tiles in the app.
Inputs the prompt needs: Tile and adhesive type; sample recordings.

Task: Bull marking for flooring along with Colour and pattern for tiles having been approved by Customer and surface preparation
QC check: Pattern of laying tiles is confirmed with the client. - work man ship
What to measure or judge: Client confirmation of the dado tile pattern recorded.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: client approval step in the app, as for ID 199.
How it would work: Same approval flow as ID 199, for the dado pattern.
Fallback or upgrade: Site-visit sign-off photo.

QC check: Scratch test has been conducted after 7 days of plastering and is found to be good.
What to measure or judge: Plaster hardness: a scratch leaves a clean line without powdering or crumbling.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: photo of the scratch mark with the tool in frame; Gemini judges powdering.
How it would work: The SE scratches the plaster with a nail or a key and photographs the mark close up; the vision model judges a clean line against powdering or flaking. The app enforces the 7-day gap from the plastering date.
Fallback or upgrade: MANUAL judgement by the SE, recorded with the photo.

QC check: Sign handover letter
What to measure or judge: Handover letter signed by the client.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: e-signature step in the app.
How it would work: An e-signature step in the app (OTP or a drawn signature on the letter). The signed document is the record.
Fallback or upgrade: Photo of the signed paper letter.

Task: Chasing for Plumbing Lines, installing Plumbing lines along with Chicken mesh complete
QC check: Surface has been prepared for tiling.
What to measure or judge: Chases filled, mesh over pipe runs, surface hacked or roughened, clean, plumbing lines in place.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: Gemini checks the sweep for filled chases, mesh over the pipe runs, a hacked surface and cleanliness.
How it would work: The vision model checks each rectified wall for filled chases, chicken mesh over the pipe runs, a hacked or roughened surface and no loose material. Pipe pressure testing is not visible and stays an ATTEST item.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP close-ups of the chases.

Task: Chasing, Conduit fixing, Door Frame Fixing, Grill Fixing and Chicken Mesh
QC check: Window grill to be checked as per the drawings and client approval
What to measure or judge: Grill design and size against the drawing; client approval recorded.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: Gemini compares the grill in the sweep with the drawing or the approved design image.
How it would work: Same spec-match detector as ID 125: the vision model compares the grill in the sweep with the drawing or the approved design image; size from the rectified wall. The approval is an ATTEST step.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP close-up of the grill.
Inputs the prompt needs: Grill drawing or approved design image.

Stage: Casting the lintels,staircase, blockwork upto the slab level
QC check: Workmanship of the blockwork is as per standards
What to measure or judge: Bond pattern (no continuous vertical joints), filled joints, broken or chipped blocks, clean faces.
(your free-text approach column): Suggested: Gemini scores the blockwork in the sweep against a workmanship rubric, per wall.
How it would work: The vision model scores each rectified wall against a workmanship rubric: staggered vertical joints, joints fully filled, no broken blocks, no mortar smears. Straightness and joint thickness are covered by IDs 31 and 36.
Fallback or upgrade: TAP close-ups where the model is unsure.
